cohort: Infants enrolled in the A.MA.MI study, with 61 fecal samples collected at baseline (meconium) and 53 fecal samples collected at six months of age.
finding: The study found that at six months of age, no single factor distinctly affects infant gut microbiota development, but rather a complex multifactorial interaction between maternal and neonatal factors determines a unique microbial niche, with specific observations regarding feeding type and siblings.
